about.title: Personal Injury Help in Lemon Grove, California
about.longDescription: Lemon Grove is a small, tight-knit city, but its roads carry a lot of traffic every day. In the most recent reported year, the city logged 52 injury collisions, 78 people hurt, and 5 traffic deaths — numbers that touch families across town. Public crash records show activity clustering along SR-94, Massachusetts Avenue, Lemon Grove Avenue, and Broadway, with Friday afternoons between 5 and 7 p.m. showing up often in the reports. If you or someone you love was hurt on one of these roads, or anywhere else in Lemon Grove, sorting out medical bills, lost wages, and insurance calls can feel like too much on top of recovering physically. LawProactive is a free service — we are not a law firm — that connects injured people with an independent personal injury attorney in the area. There's no fee unless your attorney recovers money for you. We simply help you find someone who can look at what happened and explain your options, so you're not trying to figure this out alone while you heal.

whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: You Have Time, But Not Forever
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a claim, though claims against a government agency can require notice in as little as six months. Talking to an attorney early helps make sure you don't miss a deadline.

items.title: Partial Fault Doesn't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your share of fault simply reduces the amount you might receive, it doesn't eliminate it.

items.title: No Ceiling on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain, suffering, and loss of enjoyment of life. That means your claim isn't artificially limited to just medical bills and lost wages.

items.title: You Don't Pay Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to hire one. They only get paid if you win or settle your case.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in California?
items.answer: In most cases, California law gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government entity was involved, such as a city vehicle or a road maintenance issue, the deadline can be much shorter, sometimes just six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means being partly at fault doesn't bar you from recovering compensation. Your percentage of fault would reduce the amount you might receive, but it wouldn't eliminate your claim entirely.
